acceptance_criteria.evidence:
MET ON origin/main INDEPENDENTLY OF PR #12988, and then strengthened by it.

The beat carries all three named consumers, bounded, at its own slow cadence: internal/agent/report.go SpaceReport (:394-) carries SitesDir/SitesBytes/SitesTop (per-slug du, capped at sitesTopLimit=10), PGSizeBytes/PGTopRelations (pg_total_relation_size, LIMIT 10 — never a du over PGDATA), and JournalBytes (`journalctl --disk-usage`, a header read, not a tree walk). Every probe is separately bounded (dfProbeTimeout / journalProbeTimeout / duProbeTimeout via boundedSpaceRunner) and the walk runs `nice -n 19 ionice -c3 du -hx -d1` as DIRECT argv — measuring pressure must not add it. It rides internal/agent/agent.go's SEPARATE 15-minute cycle (DefaultSpaceInterval, :24), never the 60s beat.

WHAT PR #12988 ADDS, because the criterion says BOUNDED and a bound that cannot announce itself is the hazard: SpaceReport.SitesCount now reports how many slugs the walk FOUND, not how many survived the cap. Ten slugs and a total read identically whether the tree holds ten or forty. The cap moved from parseDuTree to gatherSpace (the payload boundary) so the denominator survives; -1 stays unmeasured, never a 0 claiming an empty tree. TestSitesCountSaysWhenTheCapBinds pins all three states; mutation-proven (dropping the count assignment reds it by name, restored green).

SEPARATELY, and the reason this row's own framing said the breakdown 'still requires an SSH session': the beat carried it and NOTHING SERVED IT. Telemetry.normalize_space/1 had no production caller — verified by `git grep normalize_space origin/main` returning only its own definition, a router COMMENT, and its unit tests. PR #12988 adds Metrics.space/1 as that caller, so the sites tree + postgres + journal now reach GET /v1/barkparks/:id/metrics. Proven over real HTTP in metrics_route_test.exs "what the agent POSTs to /v1/agent/space is served by GET /metrics"; mutation-proven (nil'ing the route's fetch reds 3 tests by name).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: RESIDUE — JOB 2 (c): the Console renders a box that is STRUGGLING as struggling, with the numbers, before it starts 500ing. That is the owner's own finished experience ('we should be easily able to diagnose trouble in the Barkpark Cloud') and it is the half no route yet satisfies. The clause 'the Console renders' is now true of a MERGED Console, not merely demonstrated code — which is why this waited for the merge rather than being stamped on the rendered output alone. THE SURFACE, rendered from the shipped app.js through the same node:vm seam the harness uses, at guerrilla's measured state: 'This box is struggling / swap 93% memory 92% load 2.02 per core disk 75% / What's using the disk, measured 12m ago / /opt/barkpark/sites 4.1 GB, top 4 of 8 sites / Database 3.4 GB / Journal 3.7 GB'. Numbers present, struggle named, before it starts 500ing. THE CAP FINDING IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: parseDuTree sorted the slugs, truncated to 10, and THREW THE REST AWAY WITH NO SIGNAL. The payload carried a total and ten rows, which read IDENTICALLY whether the tree held ten or forty — and those imply different operator actions. Now SpaceReport.SitesCount reports how many slugs the walk FOUND rather than how many survived, and the Console renders 'top 10 of 37 sites' or 'all 8 sites' and claims NEITHER when the count is absent: an unknown cap state must not render as an un-bound list. Boundary contract named explicitly — rows past the top 10 by bytes are DROPPED, not refused and not queued, and the drop is counted and stated. The bound stays 10 for its original reason (compressed jsonb crosses Postgres's 2032-byte TOAST threshold between 20 and 25 realistic slugs). AND THE CAP WAS MOVED from the probe to the payload boundary, on a reason worth recording: capped upstream, the only available denominator is the capped list itself — the same number under both readings. A CAP THAT EATS ITS OWN DENOMINATOR CAN NEVER ANNOUNCE ITSELF. The same discipline runs through the verdict block: -1 stays 'we did not measure' and never 0 (which claims an empty tree), measured/of always travel, and NOTHING MEASURED IS 'unknown', NEVER 'calm' — absence of a reading rendered as a good reading was the original bug. 12 mutations, each red BY NAME and restored green, each verified on disk before running. FILED 2026-08-06 from the owner's own words: "we should be able to also see what that is taking up space etc via the Cloud - we should be easily able to diagnose trouble in the Barkpark Cloud." Plus their chosen repair: cap concurrent site builds (Option 1 over buying a bigger box).

GROUND TRUTH, measured this morning on guerrilla (157.180.90.121, 2 vCPU / 3.8 GB):
  swap 1904/2047 MB (93%) · free mem 293 MB · FOUR builds running on two cores · disk 75%
  disk consumers: sites tree 4.1G (search-ember 667M, search 628M, search-capstone 585M, next-proof 577M, next-capstone 577M, nodeproof 435M, astro-search 349M, perfect-proof 150M) · postgres 3.4G · JOURNAL 3.7G · api build 68M
  deploys since the wave-1 fixes: 511 total — 214 live (41%) / 203 failed (39%) / 89 deferred (17%). Top failure: 76x HTTP 500 = the DBConnection-timeout-under-swap-thrash class (task-cbde37238506ed7c). Second: 67x Turbopack on search-capstone alone.

TWO JOBS, in the owner's priority order:

JOB 1 — CAP CONCURRENT BUILDS FLEET-WIDE. #9615 made "one active production build per SITE" a DB law; four DIFFERENT sites still build at once and that is what fills swap and 500s the API. The engine already bounds a single build (systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax -p CPUQuota, site-deploy-node.sh:17); what is missing is a fleet gate on how many run together. A capped-out build must become a COUNTED, VISIBLE deferral that re-fires (the #9615 vocabulary), never a dropped or failed row — the standing law on re-bucketing applies.

JOB 2 — DIAGNOSIS IN THE CLOUD, NO SSH. The agent already beats disk_used_percent home every 60s (internal/agent/report.go:54-56, injectable probes; router.ex:7202 stores vitals off the beat). The gaps, measured: (a) the beat carries NO swap, NO load, NO memory — the three numbers that explained every 500 this week; (b) nothing reports WHAT eats the space — the du breakdown above took an SSH session; (c) the Console renders no diagnosis surface for any of it. The finished experience, in the owner's words: see what is taking up space via the Cloud, easily diagnose trouble. That means: the beat carries swap/load/mem/disk + a bounded top-N directory breakdown (sites tree, postgres, JOURNAL — 3.7G of journal is itself a finding: nobody set a retention cap); the fleet API exposes it; bp cloud status and the Console show a box that is STRUGGLING as struggling, with the numbers, before it starts 500ing. Wire it into the existing vitals seam — extend, do not invent a second beat.

BOUNDS: any du/journalctl the agent runs must be BOUNDED (timeout / RuntimeMaxSec) — task-e05c4e4cea2282e5 is what an unbounded diagnostic did to this exact box. And the probe must never make the patient sicker: a du over 4.1G on a thrashing box belongs on a slow cadence, not the 60s beat.

BOUNDS: any du/journalctl the agent runs must be BOUNDED (timeout / RuntimeMaxSec) — task-e05c4e4cea2282e5 is what an unbounded diagnostic did to this exact box. And the probe must never make the patient sicker: a du over 4.1G on a thrashing box belongs on a slow cadence, not the 60s beat.

WAVE 5 STATUS (2026-08-06). This is the GOAL row for the owner's wish, published under charter D77 after it sat as an unpublished draft that the ready queue was nevertheless handing out. Its three clauses stand at:
* CLAUSE 3 (cap concurrent builds) -- BUILT. PR #9827 refuses at the DOOR with a typed `box_at_capacity` 409; charter D73 discharges its Sobelow hold by CI run and the PR is MERGEABLE/CLEAN with zero failing checks. It waits on ONE human: the independent second review of the door-vs-unit race.
* CLAUSE 2 (see a struggling box as struggling) -- IN FLIGHT as `dr-w5-s1` + `dr-w5-s2` + `dr-w5-s4`. Every input reaches the wire today and NOTHING consumes it: `bp cloud status` returns guerrilla `ok / rank 8 / healthy` while load15 reads 1.89-2.02x per core, swap is 92.9% full and the box answered 6,472 HTTP 500s in eight hours.
* CLAUSE 1 (see what is taking up space) -- IN FLIGHT as `dr-w5-s3` + `dr-w5-s5`. The agent measures space perfectly and POSTs it to a route that does not exist; and the design as drawn would name 2.85% of the problem on jarl, the one box actually at 95%.

This row closes when a human opening the Cloud can see all three without an SSH session.
WAVE 20 ADDENDUM — THIS ROW NOW HAS A USER-FELT NUMBER BEHIND IT (charter D350), and it is the lever aimed squarely at that number.

NOTHING CAPS CROSS-SITE BUILD CONCURRENCY TODAY, and the config comment that looks like it does, does not. cloud/config/config.exs:226 sets `site_deploy: 1` with a comment claiming "Concurrency 1 so the debounced auto-deploy enqueue+start step is serial per box" — but AutoDeployWorker's start_and_report returns :ok on {:ok, :started} ("Production: the supervised driver is running"), so the Oban job COMPLETES in seconds while the build runs for minutes. The queue serialises STARTS. And the box lock at site-deploy.sh:1770 is `/var/lock/barkpark-site-deploy-$SITE_SLUG.lock` — PER-SITE. So the flock serialises same-site and NOTHING serialises five different sites.

MEASURED CONCURRENCY, reconstructed from every run's own started_at/finished_at in /opt/barkpark/.bp-site-deploy-runs/*.terminal.json (964 runs, 2026-08-06T11:31Z..08-08T00:01Z): peak 6 concurrent builds; >=2 concurrent for 12.03% of wall time; >=3 for 8.02%; 32.4% of runs overlap a DIFFERENT site's run. Build duration p50 52s, p95 250s, max 445s — which also corrects charter D44's premise that a site build takes 2-4 MINUTES.

THE HARM, measured on the box's own 48,942-row search_intel_events series (validated by matching a searchEventId from a call taken deliberately), bucketed by the concurrency in force at each event's timestamp, over 4,280 POST-nicing documents-api events: p50 1,246ms at 0 concurrent builds -> 3,585ms at 1 -> 8,631ms at >=2. A 6.9x blow-up. The confound runs the wrong way for the null: the concurrency-0 bucket carries the HEAVIEST queries (median 1,621 results vs 674), and the effect survives banding on result_count in 3 of 4 bands.

AND NICING DOES NOT FIX IT, because the unfenced resource is MEMORY, not CPU. Both engines are niced (`nice -n 19 ionice -c3`, proven inherited on a live build). nice/ionice bound CPU share and IO priority; they do not bound page cache. Postgres on guerrilla runs shared_buffers=128MB with effective_cache_size=4GB on a 3,819MB box that is already swapping (812MB used; 259,692,683 pages in / 372,074,606 out since boot), at a 98.527% hit ratio over 1,114,474,795 block reads. `npm ci` writing node_modules evicts exactly the cache Postgres is configured to depend on.

CAUTION, so this is not over-sold: the correlation is OBSERVATIONAL, not an intervention — no build storm was forced (that would be a prod mutation). Builds cluster on publish bursts, and publish bursts also mean write load on the same Postgres, so some of the 6.9x may be co-caused. A clean A/B needs a deliberate build storm on a quiet box. Do NOT quote the pre/post-nicing aggregate (1,147ms -> 3,161ms); it is mix-confounded by ~16x corpus and traffic growth across the boundary.

RELATED, filed this wave: dr-w20-hg-demand-cut-is-the-owners-call (the ruling this cap is one of four doors to) and dr-w20-bl-debounce-window-live-experiment (the cheapest reversible test of the same threshold).
